metadata.summary: In 2025 Hull KR became just the fifth team to win the Super League Grand Final in the 30 years of the competition.
metadata.content: Willie Peters era at Hull KR ends after eliminator loss: 'Thank you for the memories, I will miss you dearly' | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Willie Peters era at Hull KR ends after eliminator loss: 'Thank you for the memories, I will miss you dearly' Hull KR will not defend their Betfred Super League title at Old Trafford after losing to Warrington in the eliminators; It brings an end to Willie Peters' four-year reign at the Robins in which he helped them to a historic treble Saturday 19 September 2026 20:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Willie Peters reflects emotionally on his four years at Hull KR after his final game in charge, before leaving to become the inaugural head coach of NRL newcomers, the PNG Chiefs In 2025 Hull KR became just the fifth team to win the Super League Grand Final in the 30 years of the competition. That was thanks to the guidance of Willie Peters. In his third year in charge of the club, he helped them 'climb Everest' and make history. Not only did they win the Betfred Super League, they picked up the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup, and then topped that off with a World Club Challenge win over Brisbane Broncos. messages.text: The Blaze beat Hampshire in final-ball thriller to secure domestic treble

metadata.summary: The Blaze secured a domestic treble by edging a last-ball thriller with Hampshire to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup women’s competition.
metadata.content: Metro Bank One Day Cup women's final: The Blaze beat Hampshire in final-ball thriller to secure domestic treble | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Metro Bank One Day Cup women's final: The Blaze beat Hampshire in final-ball thriller to secure domestic treble Emma Jones hit an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls for The Blaze and scored the winning runs off the final ball of the match in Southampton after Tammy Beaumont and Georgia Elwiss had recorded half-centuries against Hampshire for whom Ella McCaughan top-scored with 78 By ECB Reporters Network Saturday 19 September 2026 19:10, UK Image: Emma Jones (right) leaves the field with Tammy Beaumont after hitting the winning runs for The Blaze in the One Day Cup final The Blaze secured a domestic treble by edging a last-ball thriller with Hampshire to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup women’s competition. The Trent Bridge-based side had already lifted the Vitality Blast and Vitality T20 County Cup but were forced to dig deep after needing 17 from the last two overs and then two off the final ball. Emma Jones was the hero with an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls and scored the winning runs - after Tammy Beaumont and Georgia Elwiss had scored half-centuries in the chase of 252.
